# Queue List Scope

## How To Build

A QueueListScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A QueueListScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../../ui/theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Concept

### Pitch

The tasks waiting their turn while the harness works, listed above the chat input, where they can be reordered, edited, or cancelled before they are sent.

### Shape

#### Description

The queue holds the tasks sent while the harness is working, as the [PromptSendingScope](../sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says, in the order they were sent unless they have been moved since, and sends them one at a time, first to last.

#### Placement

The queue sits along the bottom of the view, below the output and directly above the chat input, with a border along its top. It is not part of the header. A row saying how many prompts are queued, with a chevron, expands to list each queued prompt in order, a line or two of each, with a button to cancel it. Each prompt in the list is numbered, with its number, text, and cancel button vertically centred in its row, and the list scrolls once it gets tall, with a [ScrollbarScope](../../../ui/components/scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope). Each time it is expanded, it opens scrolled to the bottom, on the prompts queued most recently, however it was scrolled when last closed. The same area holds the auto-send switch and the "Send next" button. The queue is shown only while it has anything in it.

#### Cancel

A queued prompt that has not been sent yet can be cancelled, which removes it from the queue for good. A prompt already sent is no longer in the queue.

#### New Conversation

Each queued prompt in the list has a small ghost button with a sparkles icon, first of its buttons, shown as selected while the prompt will start a new conversation rather than carry on the tasks', as its hidden anchor records, as the [ChatInputScope](../chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says. Clicking it switches between the two, saving the prompt again with the project. Its tooltip says which the prompt does, and that clicking does the other instead. The choice stays with the prompt wherever it is moved in the queue.
The toggle can only make a prompt start a new conversation; it can't bring back one that was left. Once New conversation has been pressed for the tasks, the next task to run starts a new conversation whichever prompt it is, even when the prompt it marked has been moved further down or switched back to carrying on.

#### Reorder

After the new conversation button, each queued prompt in the list has two small ghost buttons, one with an up chevron, whose tooltip says it moves the prompt up, and one with a down chevron, whose tooltip says it moves the prompt down. Each swaps the prompt with its neighbour above or below it, and the order is saved with the project, so the queue comes back in its new order when the project is opened again. Move up is disabled on the first prompt and move down on the last, and both are disabled while either prompt they would swap is still being saved, as its spinner shows. A prompt being edited can still be moved, and the chat input's "Editing queued prompt N" follows it to its new place. A move that can't be saved leaves the queue as it was, and a notification titled "Could not move the prompt" says why.

#### Editing

Each queued prompt in the list also has a button with a pencil icon, after its move buttons and before its cancel button, whose tooltip says it edits the prompt. Clicking it edits the prompt in the [ChatInputScope](../chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope), as it says, and its row is highlighted while it is being edited. While it is, it is held where it is: it is never sent, and a queue waiting on it waits, even with auto-send on. Saving the edit puts the new text, in the mode and with the attachments it was saved with, in its place in the queue, saved with the project in place of what it held, then lets the queue go on as before. An edit that can't be saved leaves the prompt as it was, and a notification titled "Could not save the queued prompt" says why. Cancelling the edit, or cancelling the prompt from the list meanwhile, leaves the queue as it was, less that prompt when it was cancelled.

#### Queueing On Purpose

A prompt queued on purpose from the chat input's send menu, while the harness is free, waits at the end of the queue rather than being sent at once: it goes when "Send next" is clicked, or when the next task is over and auto-send is on.

#### Auto Send

A "Send next automatically" switch picks between sending the next queued prompt as soon as the harness is free, and waiting. It starts switched on. Switching it on while the harness is free sends the next queued prompt straight away. Whenever the harness is free and the queue is not empty, a "Send next" button sends the first queued prompt.

#### Persistence

Queued prompts are saved with the project's data as they are queued, as the [ProjectDataScope](../../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says. The queue is restored the first time the project is opened in a launch; a restored queue waits for "Send next" rather than sending on its own. A queued prompt's file is removed when it is cancelled, or when it is sent, at which point it is saved to the prompt history like any other prompt.

Both changes are in the queue list's rows (`render_queue` in `src/prompt_mode.rs`). It builds, and the existing queue, queued-prompt and new-conversation tests pass. I haven't run the app to look at it, and no test checks the line.

- **New-conversation toggle:** the sparkles ghost button is now an extra-small toggle slider. It's still the first control in each row and is on while the prompt will start a new conversation. Its tooltips and click behaviour are unchanged, and it keeps its old element id (`new-conversation-queued`).
- **Shared-context line:** each row now has a narrow gutter on its left. A 1px line in the theme's border colour joins a prompt to the one below it when that prompt carries on the same conversation. A small dot marks each prompt that's part of a joined group. Prompts that start a new conversation begin a new group, and a prompt on its own gets no mark.
  - To make the line run unbroken from row to row, I replaced the 4px gap between rows with 2px padding above and below each row, so the spacing looks the same.

The first queued prompt isn't drawn as connected to the conversation that's currently running; the line only joins queued prompts to each other.

The constraints file is at `.suspense/history/1790706674-Prompt_d56ae62ed6958318.understanding.md`.

The spec hasn't caught up: `spec/scope/prompt-mode/queue-list/index.pi` still describes "a small ghost button with a sparkles icon" and doesn't mention the line. I left it alone as you asked, so it will need updating to match.
